input: Build a monthly cash envelope system for spending

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing which spending categories to include (groceries, dining, entertainment, etc.) determines how many envelopes are needed and how the system is structured.
Whether this is physical cash envelopes, a digital app, or a hybrid approach completely changes the tools and setup process.
A solo system vs. one shared with a partner or family changes how money is divided, accessed, and tracked.
The total monthly budget available to allocate sets the foundation for all envelope amounts.
Whether the priority is strict discipline, flexibility, or simplicity affects how rigid the envelope rules should be (e.g., can money move between envelopes?).
Knowing where the user currently stands — no system at all vs. an existing budget — determines where to start.
Understanding the main problem being solved (overspending, lack of visibility, saving for goals) shapes what a successful system actually looks like.

gold.taskTitle: Build a monthly cash envelope spending system
gold.taskDescription: Set up a cash envelope budgeting system to allocate and manage monthly spending across different categories.

questions.title: Which spending categories do you want envelopes for?
questions.description: Identify the specific budget categories to be covered — e.g., groceries, dining out, gas, entertainment, personal care — so the right number of envelopes and labels are created.

questions.title: Will this be physical cash, a digital tool, or both?
questions.description: Determine the format of the system — literal paper envelopes with cash, a budgeting app like YNAB or Goodbudget, or a combination — as this dictates the entire setup process.

questions.title: Is this system just for you or shared with others?
questions.description: Clarify whether a partner, spouse, or family members are involved, which affects how cash is distributed, who controls each envelope, and how tracking is coordinated.

questions.title: What is your total monthly spending budget to allocate?
questions.description: Establish the total dollar amount available each month for discretionary spending, which is the baseline needed to divide funds across all envelopes.

questions.title: How strict should the rules be when an envelope runs out?
questions.description: Decide whether spending must stop when an envelope is empty, or if borrowing from other envelopes is allowed — this defines the discipline level and flexibility of the system.

questions.title: Do you have an existing budget or are you starting from scratch?
questions.description: Find out whether the user already tracks spending or has a budget in place, so the plan can either build on existing data or start with an initial spending audit.

questions.title: What problem are you most hoping this system solves?
questions.description: Identify the primary pain point — such as overspending in specific areas, not knowing where money goes, or saving more consistently — to ensure the system is designed around the right outcome.
